name: Scheffau am Wilden Kaiser
kurzbeschreibung: Gateway to the Wilder Kaiser, featuring the adjacent Skiwelt ski area and the Hintersteiner See.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Scheffau am Wilden Kaiser is situated in the Kufstein district at an elevation of 745 metres directly beneath the south-western cliffs of the Wilder Kaiser mountain range, home to around 1,550 inhabitants. The village nestles on a sloping mountain terrace between Söll and Ellmau, extending up to the rugged peaks of the Scheffauer (2,111 m) and Sonneck (2,260 m). Celebrated as the most tranquil and authentic community within the Wilder Kaiser holiday region, Scheffau is adorned with historic hereditary farmsteads and vibrant flower displays. As Tyrol's first certified Kneipp wellness village, it harmoniously blends alpine healing with direct access to Lake Hintersteiner See and the SkiWelt network.

Geschichte

The name Scheffau stems from Middle High German words meaning sloping water meadow. The settlement was first documented in 1160 as Seefenouwen in records of the Admont Benedictine Abbey. For centuries governed by Bavarian dukes, Scheffau became permanently Tyrolean in 1504 following Emperor Maximilian I's campaign in the War of the Succession of Landshut. The parish church of Saint John the Baptist retains a 47-metre Late Gothic spire dating from the 15th century. In 1756, the nave received its baroque interior, highlighted by ceiling frescoes painted by Kitzbühel artist Matthias Kirchner. In the hamlet of Hinterstein, the 17th-century Bärnstatt Chapel reflects ancient local pilgrimage traditions.

Anreise

Scheffau am Wilden Kaiser offers straightforward accessibility. Drivers travel along the Inntalautobahn A12 and take the Kufstein-Süd or Wörgl-Ost exit, continuing along the B178 Loferer Straße for 15 to 20 minutes directly to the village. Rail travellers arrive at the international express stations of Kufstein or Wörgl main station. From both hubs, VVT regional bus lines 865 and 866 operate frequently. With the regional Wilder Kaiser guest card, visitors enjoy free transport on public buses, the seasonal KaiserJet hiker shuttle, and the dedicated Lake Hintersteiner See bus.

Tipps

A pristine highlight is Lake Hintersteiner See (883 m), a 56-hectare crystal-clear mountain lake fed by underground springs, offering a lido and a panoramic 5-kilometre circular trail. Families take the Brandstadlbahn gondola up to 1,650 metres to the KaiserWelt mountain adventure park, featuring treehouses, wooden obstacle courses, and trails to Lake Jochstub'nsee. In the valley, the Kneipp nature trail provides outdoor salt-inhalation cabins and reflexology paths. Walkers can explore the dramatic Rehbach Gorge with its suspension footbridges and an accessible 16th-century mine tunnel. During winter, the Brandstadlbahn provides immediate access to over 270 kilometres of groomed ski runs in the SkiWelt.
